So the number of \(G_m\)-orbits in \(\mathcal C_m\) is constant for all \(m\ge 3\), equal to \(632\).

Sketch of the self-contained count: reduce modulo \(8\). For \(m\ge 3\), simultaneous conjugacy classes of commuting involution pairs over \(\mathbb Z/2^m\mathbb Z\) are in bijection with those over \(\mathbb Z/8\mathbb Z\). This follows by lifting one 2-adic level at a time: if
\[
A^2=B^2=I,\qquad AB=BA
\]
holds modulo \(2^r\) with \(r\ge 3\), the correction terms modulo \(2^{r+1}\) satisfy a linear system over \(\mathbb F_2\), and conjugation by matrices congruent to \(I\) modulo \(2^{r-1}\) kills exactly the ambiguity. Thus no new orbit data appears beyond modulo \(8\).

It remains to count the orbits for \(G_3=GL_2(\mathbb Z/8\mathbb Z)\). By Burnside,
\[
\#(\mathcal C_3/G_3)
=\frac1{|G_3|}\sum_{g\in G_3} |\mathcal C_3^g|.
\]
Here
\[
|G_3|=|GL_2(\mathbb F_2)|\cdot 2^{8}=6\cdot 256=1536.
\]

For each conjugacy class of \(g\), \(\mathcal C_3^g\) is the set of commuting involution pairs inside the centralizer of \(g\). The finite centralizer audit over \(\mathbb Z/8\mathbb Z\) gives the following grouped data:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
\text{total elements }g & |\mathcal C_3^g| & \text{contribution}\\
\hline
672 & 64 & 43008\\
512 & 64 & 32768\\
96 & 256 & 24576\\
72 & 1024 & 73728\\
32 & 1024 & 32768\\
24 & 1408 & 33792\\
96 & 4096 & 393216\\
12 & 10240 & 122880\\
4 & 10240 & 40960\\
12 & 10624 & 127488\\
4 & 11392 & 45568
\end{array}
\]

The total contribution is
\[
970752.
\]
Therefore
\[
\#(\mathcal C_3/G_3)=\frac{970752}{1536}=632.
\]

Hence, for every integer \(m\ge 3\),
\[
\boxed{632}.
\]
